mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates broader economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with sustained increases in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month indicates a contraction in the supply side of the economy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the immediate negative economic signal.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a single month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k & UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a single month indicates a weakening demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a single month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over a 3-month period signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates broader economic growth and increased corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with sustained increases in GDPC1.
